allowed_dependency_manifest.content: Fix an integer n greater than 1. Let f_n(x) = floor(n times x) minus the sum for integer k from 1 to n of floor(k times x) divided by k. Consider f_n as a function on all real numbers x. Determine all real x values at which f_n(x) is globally maximal, and determine the corresponding maximal value M(n) = max over real x of f_n(x).
allowed_dependency_manifest.label: root_semantic_sketch

forbidden_claims.statement_nl: Let $n$ be an integer greater than 1. For which real numbers $x$ is \\[\\lfloor nx \\rfloor - \\sum_{k=1}^{n} \\frac{\\lfloor kx \\rfloor}{k}\\] maximal, and what is the maximal value that this expression can take?

statement_nl: For every integer n>1 and every real t with 1 - 1/n <= t < 1, one has floor(k*t) = k - 1 for every integer k with 1 <= k <= n; consequently, f_n(t) = H_n - 1.
